comment: Hot replaceable module manifest. Sources compile into the coarse mimita-game DLL; headers participate in change detection and code hashing. 'cold' lists EXE-owned sources whose changes cannot be activated live (HOT_RELOAD_BOUNDARY_VIOLATION). 'bridges' lists EXE-owned dispatch-only bridges: their behavior already lives in a hot header/provider, they contain no policy, and a change still requires a cold relink (HOT_RELOAD_BRIDGE_CHANGE).
comment_legacy: LEGACY / STABLE-KERNEL. These EXE-owned files are kept in place (never deleted) and are not hot-reloadable by design. Their retry/session/policy now lives behind hot capabilities; what remains is OS/thread/lifetime mechanism, a dispatch bridge, or a thin transport wrapper whose callbacks must never enter a replaceable module. Each entry lists what stays cold and why. A change here requires a cold relink (HOT_RELOAD_LEGACY_CHANGE).

legacy.why: Cold mechanism, hot policy. Process/thread/socket lifetime, the fixed-tick accumulator loop, shutdown, and the live-code distribution announce stay cold. Tick orchestration decisions are hot (network.tick via hot-server-tick.h); mode selection and startup NPCs are hot (net.server-policy); lifecycle diagnostics route through log.event. The loop itself cannot move hot.
Thin libjuice wrapper. libjuice owns its own thread; callbacks must never enter a replaceable module. Only the generation-safe callback token + quiesceForReload drain are added here.
Wire struct layouts. The schema layer (hot-packet-schemas.h) carries versioned identities and hot codecs; the C++ layout stays the cold source of truth for the framing structs.
Packet parse/dispatch mechanism (size/source/rate gates, movement decode, spawn/ack bookkeeping). All acceptance policy is hot; the parse loop stays cold.
Cold NPC simulation host (NpcSystem mirrors, history deques, collision). Targeting/respawn/ground-clamp/lifecycle policy are hot.
Cold player storage/history/interp buffers. Spawn/respawn/broadcast-interp/rewind policy are hot.

Cold mechanism, hot policy. Projectile storage, physics/collision adapters, and packet transport stay cold. Splash/impact policy (net.projectile-splash, projectile.impact) and owner-death cancellation (net.projectile-cancel) are hot. Legacy dead branches (tickServerProjectiles/explodeProjectile/projectileConfig) are kept in place, marked legacy, and are unreachable from the live server.
Cold packet parse, weapon-state store, and body-part volume geometry. Attack gates/claim/policy are hot.
Cold contact detection/episode storage. Damage/knockback/interval policy are hot.

Cold mechanism, hot policy. Authoritative health/velocity apply, movement-impulse recording, and the reliable damage-event codec stay cold. Accept/reject, friendly-fire, clamp, death/respawn, explicit suicide (attacker==victim, no score), and kill attribution are hot (net.damage-application, net.kill-attribution). actor.damage/actor.killed/actor.respawn_requested facts emit through the generic event system.
Cold replica storage, chunk reassembly buffers, and artifact receiver. Generation/connection/input/client-snapshot policy are hot.
Cold prediction buffers and projectile presentation. Projectile-correction/rocket-flight/present policy are hot.

Cold mechanism, hot policy. UDP/ICE transport handles, the ICE connect worker, socket ownership, and teardown stay cold. Reconnect cadence and connection health (net.connection-policy) plus the join/reconnect state-machine transition, retry timing, timeout classification, and user-visible stage labels (connection.transition via hot-connection-transition.h) are hot. Lifecycle records route through log.event.
Cold state buffers and correction application. Reconciliation policy is hot (GAME_EVENT_RECONCILE).
Cold queue memory, transmission, and disconnect safety. Retry/ACK/TTL policy is hot (GAME_EVENT_NET_RELIABLE_POLICY).
